Rationale.RP1_ImplementationReconstructability: The experiment can be fully reconstructed from plan.md and CodeWalkthrough.md. The logit lens technique, evaluation metrics, and expected three-phase pattern are clearly described. The LeelaLogitLens class provides a clean interface and the demo notebook serves as a working reference.
Rationale.RP2_EnvironmentReproducibility: All dependencies are specified in pyproject.toml and install correctly. Model files (lc0-original.onnx) and datasets (puzzles.csv) are available. The leela-interp library works with PyTorch 2.9. Minor ONNX deprecation warnings do not affect functionality.
Rationale.RP3_DeterminismAndStability: Results are deterministic and stable across runs. The logit lens evaluation uses deterministic forward passes. Seed control ensures reproducible puzzle sampling. The three-phase pattern consistently appears in results matching the paper description.
Rationale.RP4_DemoPresentation: The demo.ipynb notebook can be executed standalone, demonstrates the core logit lens technique, shows layer-wise policy visualization, links to full experiment scripts, and specifies all required inputs and configurations. Results match originally reported findings.
